subject: general
question: The four circles with r cm radius are such that their centers form a square. Find the ratio of the area of ​​the square by joining the circular centers and the area of ​​the rhombus by joining the tangent points of the circle.
solution:
**Given:**

Radius of each circle (r) = r cm

Distance between centers of adjacent circles = 2r

**Formula used:**

Area of square = side²

Area of rhombus = (1/2) × d₁ × d₂

**Calculations:**

** ** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/d64339c79f23a905d18b66a6d9dfd310fe1f57d86add06ff3c1b651e5d5192e3.png] 

According to figure ABCD is a square and PQRS is a Rhombus.

Side of square = 2r

Area of square = (2r)²

⇒ Area of square = 4r²

Diagonals of rhombus = 2r

Area of rhombus = (1/2) × 2r × 2r

⇒ Area of rhombus = 2r²

Ratio of areas = Area of square : Area of rhombus

⇒ Ratio = 4r² : 2r²

⇒ Ratio = 2 : 1

**∴ The ratio of the area of the square to the area of the rhombus is 2:1.**
